thread:
anya: FYI — first pass of a Tenant Segmentation Assurance runbook for Private deployments (VPC + on‑prem). Posting here for quick review, gaps, and action items. TL;DR checks: RBAC smoke, KMS policy validation, audit-log e2e, netpol egress denial, tenant compromise sim.

anya: Runbook steps (short):
1) RBAC: create temp role 'seg-test-tenant' with minimal perms; verify no access to other tenants' storage or control-plane APIs.
2) KMS: attempt envelope decrypt using tenant key from a sandboxed node and from a different tenant node — expect failure.
3) Audit logging: generate a few ops (token create, model load, secret fetch) and confirm logs appear in tenant's audit stream and non-tenant cannot subscribe.
4) Netpol/Firewall: deny egress to management plane from tenant compute; validate BFD + connection reset on denied ports.
5) Kube / Host isolation: simulate pod escape attempt (mount svcacct token) and ensure host namespaces are sealed.
6) Compromise sim: escalate one tenant VM to root in a lab and validate lateral access is blocked.
7) Incident path: if any failure, run containment play: revoke keys, revoke RBAC, isolate node, and kick off IR chat.

anya: full tests and example commands below (very small snippets):
```
# RBAC smoke
kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:seg-test-tenant:default
# expect: no

# KMS check (pseudo)
curl -k -H 'X-Tenant: a' https://kms.internal/v1/decrypt -d '{ciphertext:...}'
# expect: 403 when called from tenant-b node
```

dmitri: thanks, good structure. couple of quick asks: add an explicit step to validate KMS key policy via the customer-managed KMS API (listGrants/listKeyPolicy) — sometimes IAM caches mask issues. also add timing for log propagation (we saw up to 15s in eu-west1).

matt: +1 on timing and add a streaming audit subscription test. make sure the test includes verifying cloudwatch/stackdriver forwarding is scoped by tenant id.

jess: for netpols — include a deterministic port sweep from a tenant pod against management subnet and assert RST/ICMP unreachable on every port. we should also test UDP flows (DNS, metrics) specifically.

ops-oncall: procedural note: any test that flips RBAC or revokes keys needs a rollback script. we should gate those steps to 'lab' environment only unless oncall is present and approves. also add a step to notify support + create a hotfix flag in console.

anya: agreed — I'll add explicit rollback snippets and a gating checkbox. Also adding a small section mapping runbook steps to escalation owners.

sec-bot: automated scan scheduled: tenant-seg-assurance-runbook v0.1 will run in staging at 2026-03-22T09:00Z. Report posted to #eng-security-reports.

dmitri: one more: add verification for prefix/KV cache isolation — a misconfigured cache could leak tokens. simple test: write a unique key under tenant A prefix from node A, try to read via node B's inference path; expect miss.

jess: include network egress to external endpoints too — some customers rely on egress proxies. test both block and allowed egress using a proxy ACL.

matt: also note we need KMS audit log correlation: make sure that decrypt attempts include principal and src-ip in the audit entry so IR can map actions to a node.

anya: thanks all. I'll update doc with: KMS policy check, log timing thresholds, cache isolation test, rollback scripts, and gating. Plan to run an initial table-top and then a staged run in staging. @ops-oncall please confirm a safe window?

ops-oncall: Confirmed — we can do a staged run Fri 2026-03-27 02:00-04:00 UTC. I'll be oncall. Please follow gating rules.

anya: perfect. will push v0.2 to the runbook repo and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
